question: Haemolytic anaemia of prematurity due to Vitamin E deficiency typically presents in preterm infants at 4–6 weeks of postnatal age and is worsened by concurrent high-dose iron supplementation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Haemolytic anaemia of prematurity secondary to Vitamin E deficiency classically presents at 4–6 weeks of life. Iron supplementation exacerbates haemolysis because iron generates reactive oxygen species that a Vitamin-E-deficient red cell membrane cannot quench.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Preterm infants have low Vitamin E stores and are prone to haemolytic anaemia at 4–6 weeks. High-dose iron supplementation generates free radicals that overwhelm limited antioxidant defences, worsening haemolysis — hence the clinical pearl to not give iron without ensuring adequate Vitamin E status.
